uncited: *   **Input:** 3D volume data stored in off-chip Voxel Memory (SDRAM), camera parameters, and transfer function lookup tables.
*   **Voxel Memory:** Consists of 16-bit wide SDRAM modules.
Data is organized into "miniblocks" of $2 \times 2 \times 2$ neighboring voxels.
Miniblocks are stored linearly but with a specific skewing pattern to ensure cache locality.
Rays are projected from each pixel on a base plane (co-planar to the volume face most parallel to the image plane).
**Voxel Fetch:** Each pipeline reads voxel data from the Voxel Memory.
*   Each pipeline is connected to its immediate neighbor by shift registers in each major unit (Interpolation, Gradient, Shading, Classification, Compositing).
*   The pipelines on the far left (Pipeline 0) and far right (Pipeline 3) are connected in a wrap-around fashion.
*   **Miniblock Skewing:** Linear skewing of miniblocks is required to guarantee that rendering pipelines always have access to four adjacent miniblocks in any of the three slice orientations.
*   **Time Complexity:** Real-time performance is achieved for $256^3$ volumes at 30 fps.
The Vg500 architecture is the core of the VolumePro system, developed by Mitsubishi Electric.
